summary: Add cookie-based sessions on top of the existing in-memory user store. No JWT, no external IdP. Login sets an HttpOnly session cookie; authenticate_user reads that cookie.

steps.title: Session store and cookie helpers
steps.description: Add a signed session id in an HttpOnly cookie, mapped to user_id in process memory. Sign with a local secret from env, not a cloud KMS.
steps.rationale: u1 must: no external identity services; prefer session cookies.

steps.title: authenticate_user from the session cookie
steps.description: def authenticate_user(request) -> User | None. Reads the cookie, looks up the session, returns the user or None. No Authorization header.
steps.rationale: This is the interface /me and other protected routes will call.

steps.title: POST /login and /logout using cookies
steps.description: login checks src/users.py, sets the session cookie, returns 204. logout clears it. /health stays open.
steps.rationale: u1 want: keep /health public. Cookie on the response, not a token body.

assumptions: A single-process server is enough for the demo; sessions do not need Redis.
Mobile clients are out of scope for u1's must-haves.
